method: Independent ordinary play from inspected JPEG captures, visible briefing, controls and HUD only; existing visible-playtest driver with bounded normal synthetic inputs and Escape pauses. No source, tests, prior reviews, hidden state or arranged evidence inspected. Two attempts completed; no further attempts.

outcomes.summary: Killed entry guard, recovered East then Heart, lost time seeking West approach behind cover; died before reaching it.
Recovered all three, returned via east aisle, entered extraction ring. HUD showed uplink 35% (JPEG 37%) and near-edge warning; died during next batch after moving slightly inward and waiting.

findings.text: Cohesive teal and amber storm station, restrained typography and attractive title/briefing/death screens provide a strong identity. Cyan archive structures and green extraction beacon are visually recognizable.

Hold-E floor-ring guidance and recovered-person cards make objective progress clear; second run successfully recovered all memories after learning receiver placement. Supply restoration supports continued movement.

Pylons draw attention but the actual receiver is offset in front. Several 3–5 m approaches produced MOVE CLOSER or generic Approach a memory receiver while the large pylon dominated view. Floor ring helps once seen.

Navigation around cover consumed much of first run. West signal behind cover and south intake/east service text gave direction but did not expose a route from that approach; second run found the clearly signed front entrance. Cover also halted forward travel until jumping.

Combat readout, multiple bearing boxes, objective guidance, memory card and extraction panels can compete for attention. Small visor glyphs and compact target text were harder to parse than large health/ammo numbers.

Second run reached extraction with 100 health / 60 shield but took heavy damage near the edge and died within roughly five mission seconds. Inward warning was useful; stationary hold was unsuccessful, and I did not establish safe use of split baffles. This does not prove unavoidable damage.

Discrete paused synthetic mouse inputs made precise optic tracking and reactive charge breaks difficult; low accuracy and zero phase evades limit combat balance conclusions. Audio enjoyment and hardware performance were not assessed. No renderer claims made.
